# Pitstops have stories too 

[[1mms69eg0e2vwaj6gx3pgmdwp9]]

A dharamshala is a peculiar kind of place: a home built for people who do not intend to stay. Its walls and roof create a temporary refuge, but its purpose is to make further journeys possible.

Cantor sounds like an accidental dharamshala. Refugees, veterans, engineers, dog walkers, children dreaming of stars. Each brings pieces of distant places, and each might unknowingly furnish someone else’s next departure.

Perhaps the pioneering spirit depends less on the courage of explorers than on the hospitality of those who stay behind.

Your daughter’s request that you accompany her to the stars introduces a delightful complication. She wants to be a pioneer without becoming a stranger.

Imagine a universe dotted not with colonies and outposts but with dharamshalas, each offering a little familiarity without demanding that travelers put down roots.

Would such a universe even need a frontier?

This reminds me of the [Karla Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Caves) in India’s Western Ghats where merchants helped establish durable places along networks of movement, enabling both religious communities and broader exchanges.
